html_source: Photograph taken by chief steward M. Linoenewald of the liner Prinz Adalbert early on 15 April 1912, hours after the Titanic struck an iceberg in the same area, with a note observing that red paint was "plainly visible" on the iceberg, apparently made by the "scraping of a vessel" on it. Titanic had a large stripe of red paint just above the waterline. Source: www.telegraph.co.uk.
